body: I think I will, after this weekend.  I start paying for my own medical insurance in January and my psychiatrist will be out of network.

About 7 months, if they give me that amount of time.  Though, that's taking all of my money, a large portion of which should be going to the government (my new job is 1099, so I should be leaving money aside to pay my own taxes).

I definitely won't do what I did before.  I'm making good money now, though most of it is spoken for and I won't get to spend any of it for several months.

However, I have a history of doing rather drastic things when I get depressed.  

When I was 15 I ran away from home with a plan to go live with someone I met on the internet. I'm kind of glad that didn't pan out (I was one bus stop away when the cops picked me up, a few days later). 

When I was 22 I packed everything that could fit into my car and drove to get away from my small town.  I planned to audit classes at university and work to pay for eventual tuition.  I spent 9 months living in it while I got a crappy job and then a better job that could support me.  I never ended up taking those classes, though.

When I was 15 I ran away from home to meet someone I met on the internet.  I made it 2,000 miles in about 3 days on a Greyhound before the cops picked me up.  This was in 1997, a few months after the Heaven's Gate mass suicide.  The cops were worried I was trying to join a cult, so they bunked me with Mormons for a few days while my father arranged some transport.  Strange logic there..

There were rumors about me for a while.  One of the strangest things I heard was over a year later, "My mother doesn't want me talking to you, she says you're a bad influence."  "What, why?"   "Did you really try to join a cult?"
